subject: Perf deep-dive & architecture review — schedule and runbook
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acme-retail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Demo this week — can we expand into an architecture/perf deep-dive?

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. We wanted to expand the conversation into a focused architecture and performance review before we commit to a Dedicated capacity pilot. A couple of asks: 

- Can we reschedule the demo to include a 60-90 minute technical deep-dive with your infra/serving engineering? We want to discuss KV cache behavior, burst capacity, and how fallbacks affect latency under load.
- Ideally we also run a short staging load run during the session so our SREs can validate token throughput and 95th percentile latency together.

Our initial availability: Tue/Wed 11/3–11/4 between 10:00–13:00 PT.

Load profile (high level):
- Typical baseline: 150 reqs/min, avg 800 tokens per req
- Peak bursts: up to 2,500 concurrent requests for 8–12 minutes during promotions
- Goal: validate sustained token throughput up to ~3,000 tokens/sec with P95 latency target < 250ms for 90% of requests

Attaching our peak pattern CSV and will loop in our devops. Can you also share any pre-call checklist so we can provision staging access?

Thanks,
Maria Gomez
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Retail

Hi Maria — this is great context, thanks.

We can definitely run a combined architecture + perf session with a short staged run. Proposed next steps:
1) 60–90 minute deep-dive (architecture, KV/embedding caching, routing, and fallbacks) + 20 minute staging run for an initial throughput sweep.
2) We'll bring the serving engineering leads (cc'd Laura & Vivek).
3) Please share the CSV and any representative payloads (we only need a couple of sample requests).

Suggested slots (PT):
- Wed 2026-11-03 10:30–12:00
- Wed 2026-11-03 11:00–12:30
- Thu 2026-11-04 10:00–11:30

I've attached our perf runbook template (redwood_perf_runbook_v1.docx) — fill the top section with the model variant, seq length distribution, and auth details for staging. For the run itself, our typical starting plan is:
- Ramp: 30s ramp to target
- Target sweep: 3k tokens/sec sustained for 10 minutes (we can shorten for initial validation)
- Metrics: P50/P95/P99 latency, token/sec, GPU utilization, kv-cache hit rate, error rate

Do any of those slots work? If so I'll send a calendar invite and Zoom link and request staging credentials from your team.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[jordan_blake@redwood.ai]

I've attached the peak_pattern.csv and a sample request payload. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- The 3k tokens/sec target is our internal upper-bound target for the staging run; if you have suggestions on a lower baseline for the first sweep, happy to follow your recommendation.
- We'll provision a staging VPC and a test client from our side (auth token will be provided to your engs during the run).

Pre-call checklist we'd like if possible:
- Staging endpoint + expected DNS name
- Auth token format and TTL requirements
- Recommended concurrency settings and any client-side retries to disable during the run
- Point person for telemetry (who will share Grafana/Prometheus links)

Thanks — see you Wed 11/3.

Maria

Perfect — I booked Wed 2026-11-03 11:00–12:30 PT and sent a Google Calendar invite (link below). Zoom will be used for the session; we'll run the staged throughput sweep at ~11:45 PT.

Zoom: https://zoom.us/j/9876543210?pwd=abc123
Calendar: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abc123def456

Run plan (short):
- 11:40 — connectivity check and telemetry links shared
- 11:45 — quick architecture walk (10–15 min)
- 11:55 — ramp to 1k tokens/sec (sanity) for 2 min
- 11:58 — ramp to 3k tokens/sec sustained for up to 10 min (collect P50/P95/P99, GPU, kv-hit)
- Post-run — 10–15 min incident review and next steps

Target SLOs to validate: P95 < 250ms, error rate < 0.5%, sustained token throughput at least 3k tokens/sec without evicting hot KV entries. If we see degradation we'll fall back to a smaller model variant or enable prefix-caching bypass to measure delta.

See you Wed — Jordan

Adding a few engineering items to prepare for the Wed session:

Quick checklist for staging (from serving eng):
- Model variant: specify base/quantized names (we need exact model ID)
- Expected max seq length and typical bucket distribution (p95 seq length)
- Sample client concurrency pattern (rps, concurrency, payload sizes)
- Confirm KV cache population strategy (warm vs cold start)
- If using Private deployment, provide KMS key id and routing IP allowlist

Experiment ideas during the run:
- A/B between float16 and int8/quantized runtime to observe latency/cost delta
- Toggle prefix/KV caching to measure hit-rate impact on P95
- Run with and without automatic batching to compare tail latency

I'll prepare kv_cache_notes.md and a few run scripts (attached) — Vivek and I will join the session and own the run orchestration.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
